subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens to the temperature of the surroundings?
options: It increases
It decreases
It stays exactly the same
It first decreases then increases
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions transfer heat energy to the surroundings, raising their temperature.

questions.q: Which of these processes is endothermic?
options: Thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate
Combustion of methane
Neutralisation of an acid by an alkali
Respiration in cells
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition takes in heat energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: Why is the breaking of chemical bonds described as an endothermic step?
options: Energy must be supplied to break bonds
Energy is released when bonds break
Bonds break without any energy change
Breaking bonds always cools the reactants
questions.explain: Breaking bonds requires an input of energy, making it an endothermic process.

questions.q: For an exothermic reaction, how does the total energy of the products compare with that of the reactants?
options: Products have less energy than reactants
Products have more energy than reactants
Products and reactants have equal energy
It depends on the activation energy
questions.explain: In an exothermic reaction the products are at a lower energy level, and the difference is released to the surroundings.

questions.q: On a reaction profile diagram, what does the activation energy represent?
options: The minimum energy needed for reactants to react
The energy released by the reaction
The energy of the products
The total energy stored in the reactants
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles must have for a reaction to occur.

questions.q: In terms of bond energies, when is a reaction overall exothermic?
options: When more energy is released making bonds than is used breaking bonds
When more energy is used breaking bonds than is released making bonds
When bond breaking and bond making use equal energy
When no bonds are broken during the reaction
questions.explain: If bond making releases more energy than bond breaking absorbs, there is a net release of energy.

questions.q: For H2 + Cl2 to 2HCl: bond energies are H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 242 and H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol. What is the overall energy change?
options: -184 kJ/mol
+184 kJ/mol
-247 kJ/mol
+678 kJ/mol
questions.explain: Bonds broken 436 + 242 = 678; bonds made 2 x 431 = 862; 678 - 862 = -184 kJ/mol.

questions.q: 50 g of water is heated by a reaction and its temperature rises by 10 degC. Using c = 4.2 J/g degC, how much energy is transferred? (Q = m c dT)
questions.explain: Q = 50 x 4.2 x 10 = 2100 J of energy transferred to the water.

questions.q: According to collision theory, a reaction occurs when particles collide with sufficient energy and:
options: the correct orientation
the same mass
the same colour
opposite electrical charges only
questions.explain: Successful collisions need both enough energy and the correct orientation of the particles.

questions.q: Which change would NOT increase the rate of a reaction between a solid and a solution?
options: Cooling the mixture down
Increasing the concentration of the solution
Using smaller pieces of the solid
Adding a suitable catalyst
questions.explain: Lowering the temperature reduces particle energy and collision frequency, decreasing the rate.

questions.q: Why does increasing the surface area of a solid reactant increase the rate of reaction?
options: More particles are exposed for collisions
The particles gain more energy
The activation energy is lowered
The reactant particles move faster
questions.explain: A larger surface area exposes more particles, increasing the frequency of successful collisions.

questions.q: How does a catalyst speed up a chemical reaction?
options: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It increases the temperature of the reactants
It increases the concentration of the reactants
It is used up, releasing extra energy
questions.explain: A catalyst offers a route of lower activation energy so more collisions are successful.

questions.q: Which statement about a catalyst is correct?
options: It is not used up during the reaction
It changes the products of the reaction
It is destroyed as the reaction proceeds
It makes the reaction more endothermic
questions.explain: A catalyst is chemically unchanged and can be recovered at the end of the reaction.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure of a reacting gas mixture increases the rate because:
options: the gas particles are closer together, so collisions are more frequent
the particles gain more activation energy
the particles change into liquids
fewer collisions occur but each is more energetic
questions.explain: Higher pressure squeezes gas particles closer together, raising the collision frequency.

questions.q: Which symbol is used to represent a reversible reaction?
options: A double half arrow (equilibrium arrows)
A single forward arrow
An equals sign
A plus sign
questions.explain: Reversible reactions are shown with the two-way equilibrium arrows.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system, which statement is true?
options: The forward and reverse reactions occur at equal rates
Both reactions have stopped completely
Only the forward reaction is occurring
The concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
questions.explain: At dynamic equilibrium the opposing reactions proceed at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.q: What is the balanced equation for the reversible reaction in the Haber process?
options: N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3
N2 + H2 to NH3
2N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3
N2 + 2H2 to 2NH3
questions.explain: Nitrogen and hydrogen combine in a 1:3 ratio to form ammonia: N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction at equilibrium, increasing the temperature will:
options: shift the position of equilibrium towards the reactants
shift the position of equilibrium towards the products
have no effect on the position of equilibrium
stop the reaction completely
questions.explain: Raising temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, shifting equilibrium back towards reactants.

questions.q: In the Haber process, N2 + 3H2 to 2NH3, increasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium towards ammonia because:
options: there are fewer gas molecules on the product side
there are more gas molecules on the product side
ammonia is a solid at high pressure
pressure has no effect on gas equilibria
questions.explain: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules (4 on the left, 2 on the right), making more ammonia.

questions.q: What effect does adding a catalyst have on the position of equilibrium?
options: No change in position, but equilibrium is reached faster
It shifts the equilibrium towards the products
It shifts the equilibrium towards the reactants
It increases the yield of product at equilibrium
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached sooner but its position is unchanged.
